instruction: Change the slide size orientation to Portrait in note-taking-strategies.pptx and save the file.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened pptx in Impress (Landscape 4:3 format as seen in screenshot 0), navigated menus, and attempted font changes in Master View. Orientation change is achievable via Slide > Slide Properties > Slide Size.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate Slide menu, access Slide Properties/Size dialog, change dimensions
metadata.failure_analysis: Agent failed on font standardization. Changing orientation to Portrait is a simpler task via Slide > Slide Properties or Slide > Slide Size, within demonstrated menu-navigation capability.
metadata.task_rationale: The presentation is currently in Landscape orientation. Changing to Portrait is a simple menu-based task (Slide > Slide Properties) that targets the reliable prefix's demonstrated menu navigation without any typing.
metadata.explanation: Getter reads the PPTX file and compares slide width vs height. Metric returns 1.0 if height > width (portrait). Initial state is Landscape (width > height as confirmed in screenshot 0), so it does not pass initially.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter correctly reads the PPTX file using python-pptx and determines orientation by comparing slide_width vs slide_height (portrait if height > width), which is the standard and accurate method.
Metric correctly compares the actual orientation string to the expected 'portrait' value and returns 1.0 on exact match.
Negative control resistance is good: initial state is confirmed Landscape (width > height), so a do-nothing agent will score 0.0.
Postconfig forces a ctrl+s save before evaluation, ensuring the getter reads the persisted file state.
The evaluator covers the primary task requirement (portrait orientation) precisely and semantically.
llm_judge_fix_suggestions: Minor: The 'save the file' sub-requirement is not independently verified — the postconfig unconditionally saves for the agent, so an agent that changed orientation but forgot to save would still pass. Consider verifying file modification time or checking a separate no-postconfig path if strict save verification is needed.
